name: Slovenia
snapshot: A near-tie in the March 2026 election ended with populist Janez Janša back as prime minister for a fourth time.
culture: Slovenia packs Alps, karst caves and a short Adriatic coast into a small country. Beekeeping is a national tradition, with painted hive panels, and the country proposed World Bee Day. Cyclists Tadej Pogačar and Primož Roglič, and basketball's Luka Dončić, are global stars. Lake Bled is a postcard icon.
society: Slovenia was the richest Yugoslav republic and the first to join the EU, in 2004, and the euro. It has low inequality and high quality of life. Janša, an ally of Orbán and Trump, has clashed with media and the EU in past terms.

story: Janez Janša has been part of Slovenian politics since he was jailed by the Yugoslav army in 1988 for exposing its secrets, an arrest that helped spark the country's independence. He went on to serve as prime minister three times and became one of Europe's most combative populists, an admirer of Trump and an ally of Orbán. When Slovenians voted him out in 2022, many assumed he was finished. In 2026, at 67, he came back.

The 22 March election was nearly a tie: Prime Minister Robert Golob's liberal Freedom Movement won 29 seats and Janša's SDS 28 (Reuters via Internazionale). Golob failed to form a government. Janša then assembled a coalition with four centre-right parties plus outside support from Resni.ca, an anti-establishment party whose leader, Zoran Stevanović, rose through protests against Janša and signed a notarised pledge never to join a Janša government (New Eastern Europe). Stevanović became speaker. On 22 May, parliament elected Janša prime minister by 51 votes to 36, making him Slovenia's oldest ever premier; his cabinet took office on 4 June, promising tax cuts and pension reform (bne IntelliNews). With Orbán gone from Hungary, Janša is now one of the few leaders of his kind left inside the EU.
briefing.power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister is elected by the 90-seat National Assembly; the directly elected president, Nataša Pirc Musar, nominates candidates and has limited powers.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Janez Janša (SDS), in office since May 2026.
